title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.

    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

"""One-off reconnaissance of the released TokenCore data files and code API."""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "repo"
DATA = REPO / "data"


def inspect_npy(path):
    print("=" * 70)
    print("NPY:", path.name, f"({path.stat().st_size} bytes)")
    arr = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)
    print("  type:", type(arr))
    try:
        obj = arr.item()
    except Exception:
        obj = arr
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        print("  dict keys:", list(obj.keys()))
        for k, v in obj.items():
            print(f"   - {k}: type={type(v).__name__}", end="")
            try:
                print(f" len={len(v)}", end="")
            except Exception:
                pass
            try:
                print(f" shape={np.asarray(v).shape} dtype={np.asarray(v).dtype}", end="")
            except Exception:
                pass
            print()
            if len(v) > 0:
                print("      first:", repr(v[0])[:300])
                print("      last :", repr(v[-1])[:300])
    else:
        print("  shape:", getattr(obj, "shape", None), "dtype:", getattr(obj, "dtype", None))
        print("  first:", repr(obj[:2])[:500])


def inspect_json(path):
    print("=" * 70)
    print("JSON:", path.name, f"({path.stat().st_size} bytes)")
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    print("  top-level type:", type(data).__name__, "len:", len(data))
    item = data[0]
    print("  item type:", type(item).__name__)
    if isinstance(item, dict):
        print("  item keys:", list(item.keys()))
        for k, v in item.items():
            s = repr(v)
            print(f"   - {k}: {type(v).__name__} -> {s[:250]}")
    elif isinstance(item, list):
        print("  item:", repr(item)[:400])
    # label-studio style?
    if isinstance(data, list) and data and isinstance(data[0], dict) and "data" in data[0]:
        print("  -> looks like Label Studio export")
        print("  data[0]['data'] keys:", list(data[0]["data"].keys()))
        ann = data[0].get("annotations")
        if ann:
            print("  annotations[0] keys:", list(ann[0].keys()))
            res = ann[0].get("result")
            if res:
                print("  result[0]:", repr(res[0])[:400])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for name in ["grammar.npy", "restaurant_review.npy", "sms_spam.npy"]:
        inspect_npy(DATA / name)
    for name in ["grammar_correction_labeled.json"]:
        inspect_json(DATA / name)
    print("=" * 70)
    print("TokenCore.py / align.py signatures:")
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
    import inspect as _inspect

    import TokenCore
    import align

    print("  TokenCore members:", [n for n, _ in _inspect.getmembers(TokenCore, _inspect.isclass)])
    print("  align members:", [n for n, _ in _inspect.getmembers(align, _inspect.isfunction)])

"""Quick stats on the released grammar benchmark (npy + json)."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "repo"
d = np.load(REPO / "data" / "grammar.npy", allow_pickle=True).item()
tokens, labels, sentences = d["tokens"], d["labels"], d["sentences"]
print("n docs:", len(tokens))
n_anom_doc = sum(1 for l in labels if any(l))
print("docs with >=1 anomalous token:", n_anom_doc)
print("normal docs:", len(tokens) - n_anom_doc)
tot_tok = sum(len(t) for t in tokens)
tot_pos = sum(sum(l) for l in labels)
print("total tokens:", tot_tok, "anomalous tokens:", tot_pos, f"rate={tot_pos/tot_tok:.4%}")
print("label value set:", sorted({v for l in labels for v in l}))
print("len(tokens)==len(labels) for all:", all(len(a) == len(b) for a, b in zip(tokens, labels)))
# sentence vs tokens consistency
mismatch = 0
for s, t in zip(sentences, tokens):
    txt = s if isinstance(s, str) else s[0]
    if " ".join(t) != txt:
        mismatch += 1
print("docs where ' '.join(tokens) != sentence:", mismatch)
# anomalous docs detail
anom = [(i, tokens[i], labels[i]) for i in range(len(labels)) if any(labels[i])]
print("\nfirst 5 anomalous docs:")
for i, t, l in anom[:5]:
    print(" ", i, list(zip(t, l)))
print("\nmax subword-ish token length (chars):", max(len(w) for t in tokens for w in t))
print("max tokens per doc:", max(len(t) for t in tokens))

# JSON cross-check
with open(REPO / "data" / "grammar_correction_labeled.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    js = json.load(f)
print("\njson docs:", len(js))
lab_counts = {}
for it in js:
    lab_counts[it["data"].get("label")] = lab_counts.get(it["data"].get("label"), 0) + 1
print("json data.label counts:", lab_counts)
# how many json items have token-level annotations beyond the whole sentence
n_multi = sum(1 for it in js if len(it["annotations"][0]["result"]) > 1)
print("json items with >1 annotation span:", n_multi)
ex = [it for it in js if len(it["annotations"][0]["result"]) > 1][:3]
for it in ex:
    print("  text:", it["data"]["text"][:90])
    for r in it["annotations"][0]["result"]:
        print("    ", r["value"]["start"], r["value"]["end"], repr(r["value"]["text"]), r["value"]["labels"])

produced by ``tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py`` from the Label Studio exports.  Each file is a
pickled dict with keys ``sentences`` (list of 1-element lists), ``tokens`` (list of word
lists) and ``labels`` (list of per-word 0/1 label lists).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List

import numpy as np

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DATA_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "repo" / "data"

# name -> (npy file, expected n_docs, expected n_anomalous_docs)
DATASETS = {
    "grammar": ("grammar.npy", 300, 30),
    "review": ("restaurant_review.npy", 1100, 50),
    "sms_spam": ("sms_spam.npy", 4518, 393),
}


@dataclass
class Doc:
    doc_id: int
    words: List[str]
    token_labels: List[int]
    sentence: str = ""
    source: str = ""

    @property
    def doc_label(self) -> int:
        # Definition 2 / R11: a document is anomalous iff it contains >= 1 anomalous token.
        return 1 if any(self.token_labels) else 0

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.words)


@dataclass
class Split:
    train: List[Doc] = field(default_factory=list)
    test: List[Doc] = field(default_factory=list)


def load_dataset(name: str, data_dir: Path | None = None) -> List[Doc]:
    """Load one released benchmark into a list of :class:`Doc`."""
    if name not in DATASETS:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown dataset {name!r}; expected one of {sorted(DATASETS)}")
    fname, exp_docs, exp_anom = DATASETS[name]
    path = (data_dir or DATA_DIR) / fname
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing released data file: {path}")
    raw = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens, labels, sentences = raw["tokens"], raw["labels"], raw["sentences"]
    if not (len(tokens) == len(labels) == len(sentences)):
        raise ValueError("sentences/tokens/labels length mismatch in released file")

    docs: List[Doc] = []
    for i, (toks, labs) in enumerate(zip(tokens, labels)):
        toks = [str(t) for t in toks]
        labs = [int(l) for l in labs]
        if len(toks) != len(labs):
            raise ValueError(f"doc {i}: {len(toks)} words but {len(labs)} labels")
        sent = sentences[i]
        sent = sent if isinstance(sent, str) else sent[0]
        docs.append(Doc(doc_id=i, words=toks, token_labels=labs, sentence=sent, source=name))

    # R10 sanity checks on the released benchmark.
    n_anom = sum(d.doc_label for d in docs)
    if len(docs) != exp_docs or n_anom != exp_anom:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{name}: released file has {len(docs)} docs / {n_anom} anomalous, "
            f"paper states {exp_docs} docs / {exp_anom} anomalous"
        )
    return docs


def split_normal_train(docs: List[Doc], seed: int = 0, train_frac: float = 0.5) -> Split:
    """Paper Sec 6.1 / R6: 50% of the *normal* documents are the training (memory-bank) set;
    the remaining normal documents plus every anomalous document form the test set."""
    normal = [d for d in docs if d.doc_label == 0]
    anomalous = [d for d in docs if d.doc_label == 1]
    n_train = int(round(len(normal) * train_frac))
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    order = rng.permutation(len(normal))
    train_idx = set(order[:n_train].tolist())
    train = [normal[i] for i in sorted(train_idx)]
    test = [normal[i] for i in range(len(normal)) if i not in train_idx] + anomalous
    return Split(train=train, test=test)


def token_label_stats(docs: List[Doc]) -> dict:
    n_tok = sum(len(d) for d in docs)
    n_pos = sum(sum(d.token_labels) for d in docs)
    return {
        "n_docs": len(docs),
        "n_anomalous_docs": sum(d.doc_label for d in docs),
        "n_tokens": n_tok,
        "n_anomalous_tokens": n_pos,
        "token_anomaly_rate": (n_pos / n_tok) if n_tok else float("nan"),
    }


def cross_check_with_label_studio_json(name: str, docs: List[Doc], data_dir: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    """Verify the .npy token/label arrays against the raw Label Studio export."""
    path = (data_dir or DATA_DIR) / f"{name}_labeled.json"
    if not path.exists():
        return {"checked": False}
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        items = json.load(f)
    n_items = len(items)
    n_doc_anom = sum(1 for it in items if int(it["data"].get("label", 0)) == 1)
    n_span_anom = 0
    for it in items:
        for ann in it.get("annotations", []):
            for r in ann.get("result", []):
                if str(r["value"]["labels"][0]) == "1":
                    n_span_anom += 1
    return {
        "checked": True,
        "json_docs": n_items,
        "json_doc_level_anomalies": n_doc_anom,
        "json_anomalous_spans": n_span_anom,
        "npy_docs": len(docs),
        "npy_doc_level_anomalies": sum(d.doc_label for d in docs),
        "npy_anomalous_tokens": sum(sum(d.token_labels) for d in docs),
    }

"""BERT-base-uncased front-end: word-level embeddings by element-wise max pooling over subwords.

This is the batched re-implementation of the front-end that ``Demo.ipynb`` hid inside
``align.extract_word_embeddings`` (one sentence per forward pass, ``is_split_into_words=True``
on the gold word list, ``[CLS]``/``[SEP]`` skipped, coordinate-wise ``np.max`` over the
subword vectors of each word).  The only difference is batching, which does not change the
per-word result because padded positions carry ``word_id is None`` and are dropped.

Paper Eq. (1) / R2 / R9:  e_token = max(e_1, ..., e_n)  element-wise.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence

import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

DEFAULT_MODEL = "bert-base-uncased"


def _resolve_device(device: Optional[str]) -> str:
    if device:
        return device
    return "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"


def load_backbone(model_name: str = DEFAULT_MODEL, cache_dir: Optional[str] = None,
                  device: Optional[str] = None):
    device = _resolve_device(device)
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=cache_dir)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=cache_dir)
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    return tok, model, device


@torch.no_grad()
def extract_word_embeddings(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    all_tokens: Sequence[Sequence[str]],
    all_labels: Optional[Sequence[Sequence[int]]] = None,
    batch_size: int = 32,
    max_length: int = 512,
    device: Optional[str] = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> List[List[Dict]]:
    """Return, for every input document, a list of
    ``{'token', 'embedding', 'label', 'subword_position'}`` dicts (one per gold word)."""
    device = _resolve_device(device)
    if all_labels is None:
        all_labels = [[0] * len(t) for t in all_tokens]
    if len(all_tokens) != len(all_labels):
        raise ValueError("all_tokens / all_labels length mismatch")

    n_docs = len(all_tokens)
    results: List[List[Dict]] = []
    n_truncated = 0
    for start in range(0, n_docs, batch_size):
        chunk_tokens = [list(t) for t in all_tokens[start:start + batch_size]]
        chunk_labels = [list(l) for l in all_labels[start:start + batch_size]]
        enc = tokenizer(
            chunk_tokens,
            is_split_into_words=True,
            return_tensors="pt",
            padding=True,
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length,
        )
        enc = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in enc.items()}
        out = model(input_ids=enc["input_ids"], attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"])
        hidden = out.last_hidden_state  # [B, L, H]

        for b in range(len(chunk_tokens)):
            word_ids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=b)
            vecs = hidden[b].float().cpu().numpy()
            groups: Dict[int, List[int]] = {}
            for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
                if wid is None:
                    continue  # [CLS] / [SEP] / [PAD]
                groups.setdefault(wid, []).append(pos)
            toks = chunk_tokens[b]
            labs = chunk_labels[b]
            sent_data = []
            for wid in sorted(groups):
                positions = groups[wid]
                if len(positions) > 1:
                    emb = np.max(np.stack([vecs[p] for p in positions]), axis=0)
                else:
                    emb = vecs[positions[0]]
                sent_data.append({
                    "token": toks[wid] if wid < len(toks) else "",
                    "embedding": emb,
                    "label": labs[wid] if wid < len(labs) else 0,
                    "subword_position": positions,
                })
            if len(sent_data) != len(toks):
                n_truncated += 1
            results.append(sent_data)
        if verbose:
            print(f"  embedded docs {start + 1}-{min(start + batch_size, n_docs)}/{n_docs}",
                  flush=True)
    if n_truncated:
        print(f"  [warn] {n_truncated} document(s) lost word units (truncation at "
              f"max_length={max_length} or empty tokenization)", flush=True)
    return results


def flatten(doc_embeddings: Sequence[Sequence[Dict]]):
    """Flatten per-document dicts into (X, y, doc_index, word_index) arrays."""
    X, y, doc_idx, word_idx = [], [], [], []
    for di, sent in enumerate(doc_embeddings):
        for wi, item in enumerate(sent):
            X.append(item["embedding"])
            y.append(int(item["label"]))
            doc_idx.append(di)
            word_idx.append(wi)
    return (np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float32), np.asarray(y, dtype=np.int64),
            np.asarray(doc_idx, dtype=np.int64), np.asarray(word_idx, dtype=np.int64))


def configure_torch_threads(n_threads: Optional[int] = None) -> int:
    if n_threads is None:
        n_threads = max(1, min(8, (os.cpu_count() or 4)))
    torch.set_num_threads(n_threads)
    return n_threads

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified ``repo/TokenCore.py``.

The authors' class is loaded straight from the released file (never edited): it builds a
``sklearn.neighbors.NearestNeighbors`` index over the normal-training token embeddings and
returns, for every test token, the distance to its nearest neighbour (paper Eq. 2 / R4).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Tuple

import numpy as np

AUTHOR_FILE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "repo" / "TokenCore.py"


def load_author_tokencore(path: Path | None = None):
    """Import the authors' TokenCore class from the released source file."""
    path = Path(path or AUTHOR_FILE)
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"authors' TokenCore.py not found at {path}")
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("authors_tokencore", path)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    if not hasattr(mod, "TokenCore"):
        raise AttributeError(f"{path} does not define a TokenCore class")
    return mod.TokenCore


class TokenCoreDetector:
    """Fit the memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3)."""

    def __init__(self, n_neighbors: int = 1, aggregation: str = "max"):
        self.cls = load_author_tokencore()
        self.model = self.cls(n_neighbors=n_neighbors, aggregation=aggregation)
        self.n_bank_ = None

    def fit(self, X_train: np.ndarray) -> "TokenCoreDetector":
        X_train = np.asarray(X_train, dtype=np.float32)
        if X_train.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"expected a 2-D token embedding matrix, got {X_train.shape}")
        self.model.fit(X_train)
        self.n_bank_ = X_train.shape[0]
        return self

    def decision_function(self, X_test: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        X_test = np.asarray(X_test, dtype=np.float32)
        scores = np.asarray(self.model.decision_function(X_test), dtype=np.float64).ravel()
        if scores.shape[0] != X_test.shape[0]:
            raise RuntimeError("detector returned a wrong number of scores")
        return scores


def sanity_checks(X_train: np.ndarray, X_test: np.ndarray, scores: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    """Direction / plumbing checks for the nearest-neighbour scoring (R4)."""
    out = {}
    # training tokens themselves must be ~0 distance from the bank (self match)
    det = TokenCoreDetector()
    det.fit(X_train)
    self_scores = det.decision_function(X_train)
    out["train_self_distance_median"] = float(np.median(self_scores))
    out["train_self_distance_max"] = float(np.max(self_scores))
    out["test_score_median"] = float(np.median(scores))
    out["test_score_mean"] = float(np.mean(scores))
    out["bank_larger_than_test"] = bool(np.median(scores) > np.median(self_scores))
    return out

"""Reproduce the TokenCore token-level results of "Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection".

Pipeline (paper Sec. 5 + Sec. 6.1):
  1. load a released TokenAD benchmark (data/<name>.npy from the authors' repo),
  2. split: 50% of the *normal* documents -> memory-bank training set; the remaining normal
     documents + all anomalous documents -> test set,
  3. BERT-base-uncased forward pass, last hidden state, [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] dropped,
  4. element-wise max pooling of subword vectors into word units aligned with the gold
     word-level annotations (Eq. 1),
  5. fit the authors' TokenCore memory bank on the normal-training token embeddings only,
  6. score every test token by its nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2),
  7. pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC + mean-aggregated document-level AUROC/AUPRC (Eq. 3).

Usage:
    python reproduce.py                       # Grammar, seed 0 (target claim C1/C2)
    python reproduce.py --datasets grammar review sms_spam
    python reproduce.py --seeds 0 1 2         # multi-seed spread
    python reproduce.py --smoke               # 10-document end-to-end smoke test
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import platform
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

import data_grammar as dg  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert as eb  # noqa: E402
import evaluate as ev  # noqa: E402
from detector import TokenCoreDetector, sanity_checks  # noqa: E402

DATASET_TITLES = {
    "grammar": "Grammar (Grammar Correction, Kaggle)",
    "review": "Restaurant Review (Google Maps reviews, authors' collection)",
    "sms_spam": "SMS Spam (kendx/NLP-ADBench sms_spam, with injected character corruption)",
}


def run_one(dataset: str, seed: int, args, tok, model, device: str) -> dict:
    docs = dg.load_dataset(dataset)
    if args.smoke:
        normal = [d for d in docs if d.doc_label == 0]
        anom = [d for d in docs if d.doc_label == 1]
        docs = normal[:8] + anom[:2]
    split = dg.split_normal_train(docs, seed=seed, train_frac=0.5)

    train_docs, test_docs = split.train, split.test
    if args.smoke:
        # force a non-degenerate split on the tiny subset
        cut = max(1, len(train_docs) // 2)
        train_docs, test_docs = train_docs[:cut], train_docs[cut:] + test_docs

    # ---- embeddings (Eq. 1: element-wise max pooling over subwords) ----
    t0 = time.time()
    train_emb = eb.extract_word_embeddings(
        model, tok, [d.words for d in train_docs], [d.token_labels for d in train_docs],
        batch_size=args.batch_size, max_length=args.max_length, device=device)
    test_emb = eb.extract_word_embeddings(
        model, tok, [d.words for d in test_docs], [d.token_labels for d in test_docs],
        batch_size=args.batch_size, max_length=args.max_length, device=device)
    embed_seconds = time.time() - t0

    X_train, y_train, _, _ = eb.flatten(train_emb)
    X_test, y_test, doc_idx, _ = eb.flatten(test_emb)

    # ---- memory bank + nearest-neighbour scoring (Eq. 2) ----
    t0 = time.time()
    det = TokenCoreDetector(n_neighbors=1)
    det.fit(X_train)
    scores = det.decision_function(X_test)
    score_seconds = time.time() - t0

    # ---- metrics ----
    n_docs = len(test_docs)
    doc_token_scores = [scores[doc_idx == i] for i in range(n_docs)]
    doc_token_labels = [y_test[doc_idx == i] for i in range(n_docs)]
    doc_labels = [d.doc_label for d in test_docs]

    res = ev.evaluate(doc_token_scores, doc_token_labels, doc_labels)
    res.update({
        "dataset": dataset,
        "seed": seed,
        "n_train_docs": len(train_docs),
        "n_test_docs": len(test_docs),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(det.n_bank_),
        "n_train_tokens": int(X_train.shape[0]),
        "n_train_anomalous_tokens": int(y_train.sum()),
        "embedding_dim": int(X_train.shape[1]),
        "embed_seconds": round(embed_seconds, 2),
        "score_seconds": round(score_seconds, 2),
        "train_token_stats": dg.token_label_stats(train_docs),
        "test_token_stats": dg.token_label_stats(test_docs),
        "all_token_stats": dg.token_label_stats(docs),
    })
    res["sanity"] = sanity_checks(X_train, X_test, scores)
    res["random_control"] = ev.random_control(doc_token_labels, seed=seed + 12345)
    return res


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--datasets", nargs="+", default=["grammar"],
                   choices=sorted(dg.DATASETS))
    p.add_argument("--seeds", nargs="+", type=int, default=[0])
    p.add_argument("--model", default=eb.DEFAULT_MODEL)
    p.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=512)
    p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=32)
    p.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--out", default=str(ROOT / "results" / "metrics.json"))
    args = p.parse_args(argv)

    t_start = time.time()
    n_threads = eb.configure_torch_threads()
    print(f"[reproduce] torch threads={n_threads} python={platform.python_version()} "
          f"numpy={np.__version__}", flush=True)

    tok, model, device = eb.load_backbone(args.model)
    print(f"[reproduce] backbone={args.model} device={device}", flush=True)

    all_results = {}
    for ds in args.datasets:
        for seed in args.seeds:
            print(f"[reproduce] === dataset={ds} seed={seed} ===", flush=True)
            res = run_one(ds, seed, args, tok, model, device)
            all_results.setdefault(ds, {})[str(seed)] = res
            print(f"  token_auroc={res['token_auroc']:.4f} token_auprc={res['token_auprc']:.4f} "
                  f"doc_auroc={res['doc_auroc']:.4f} doc_auprc={res['doc_auprc']:.4f} "
                  f"(bank={res['n_bank_tokens']} tok, test={res['n_test_tokens']} tok / "
                  f"{res['n_positive_tokens']} pos)", flush=T

"""Per-config experiment harness (does NOT touch results/metrics.json).

Runs the Grammar benchmark through several faithful variants of the released pipeline and
prints one line per (config, seed) so the sensitivity of the token-level AUROC/AUPRC can be
read off without tuning toward any printed target.

Config axes (ablated one at a time, in the order requested):
  * backend   : "align"  -> authors' repo/align.py extract_word_embeddings, verbatim
                "batched"-> src/embed_bert.py (same math, batched forward pass)
  * backbone  : bert-base-cased (what Demo.ipynb / align.py actually use)
                bert-base-uncased (what the paper's Sec 6.1 states)
  * punct     : keep punctuation word units, or drop them
  * l2norm    : raw embeddings, or L2-normalised before the nearest-neighbour search
  * token_auc : "micro" (pool all test tokens) or "macro" (mean of per-document AUROC)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import contextlib
import io
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "repo"))

import data_grammar as dg  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert as eb  # noqa: E402
import evaluate as ev  # noqa: E402
from detector import TokenCoreDetector  # noqa: E402

PUNCT = set(".,!?;:'\"()[]{}<>-–—…/\\|@#$%^&*_+=~`")


def is_punct(word: str) -> bool:
    return bool(word) and all(ch in PUNCT for ch in word)


def embed_docs(backend, model, tokenizer, device, docs, batch_size=32, max_length=512):
    """Return per-document lists of {'token','embedding','label'} dicts."""
    toks = [d.words for d in docs]
    labs = [d.token_labels for d in docs]
    if backend == "align":
        import align  # authors' file, unmodified
        buf = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
            out = align.extract_word_embeddings(
                model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, all_tokens=toks, all_labels=labs,
                model_name="bert-base-cased", device=device)
        return out
    return eb.extract_word_embeddings(
        model, tokenizer, toks, labs, batch_size=batch_size,
        max_length=max_length, device=device)


def run_config(dataset, seed, backend, backbone, punct, l2norm, token_auc,
               model, tokenizer, device, batch_size=32, max_length=512):
    docs = dg.load_dataset(dataset)
    split = dg.split_normal_train(docs, seed=seed, train_frac=0.5)
    train_docs, test_docs = split.train, split.test

    train_emb = embed_docs(backend, model, tokenizer, device, train_docs, batch_size, max_length)
    test_emb = embed_docs(backend, model, tokenizer, device, test_docs, batch_size, max_length)

    def keep(sent):
        return [it for it in sent if (punct or not is_punct(it["token"]))]

    train_emb = [keep(s) for s in train_emb]
    test_emb = [keep(s) for s in test_emb]

    X_train, y_train, _, _ = eb.flatten(train_emb)
    X_test, y_test, doc_idx, _ = eb.flatten(test_emb)
    if l2norm:
        X_train = X_train / np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(X_train, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-12)
        X_test = X_test / np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(X_test, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-12)

    det = TokenCoreDetector(n_neighbors=1)
    det.fit(X_train)
    scores = det.decision_function(X_test)

    n_docs = len(test_docs)
    doc_token_scores = [scores[doc_idx == i] for i in range(n_docs)]
    doc_token_labels = [y_test[doc_idx == i] for i in range(n_docs)]
    doc_labels = [d.doc_label for d in test_docs]

    res = ev.evaluate(doc_token_scores, doc_token_labels, doc_labels)
    if token_auc == "macro":
        per_doc = []
        for s, l in zip(doc_token_scores, doc_token_labels):
            if len(np.unique(l)) == 2:
                per_doc.append(ev.safe_auc(l, s))
        res["token_auroc"] = float(np.mean(per_doc)) if per_doc else float("nan")
        res["n_docs_with_both_classes"] = len(per_doc)
    return res

    p.add_argument("--seeds", nargs="+", type=int, default=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4])

"""Shared TokenCore pipeline: data -> split -> embeddings -> memory bank -> metrics.

Two interchangeable embedding front-ends, both producing *identical* numbers:

  * ``backend="align"``   -> the authors' unmodified ``repo/align.py::extract_word_embeddings``
                             (one document per forward pass, exactly as ``Demo.ipynb`` drives it)
  * ``backend="batched"`` -> ``src/embed_bert.py`` (same math, batched forward pass)

The two were verified to agree to ~1e-4 on every seed of the Grammar benchmark; the batched
path is used wherever speed matters and the authors' helper is used for the primary run and
for the parity check.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import io
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "repo"))

import data_grammar as dg  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert as eb  # noqa: E402
import evaluate as ev  # noqa: E402
from detector import TokenCoreDetector  # noqa: E402

PUNCT = set(".,!?;:'\"()[]{}<>-–—…/\\|@#$%^&*_+=~`")

_BACKBONES: Dict[str, tuple] = {}


def is_punct(word: str) -> bool:
    return bool(word) and all(ch in PUNCT for ch in word)


def load_backbone(backbone: str):
    """Load (tokenizer, model, device) once per backbone and cache it."""
    if backbone not in _BACKBONES:
        t0 = time.time()
        tok, model, device = eb.load_backbone(backbone)
        _BACKBONES[backbone] = (tok, model, device)
        print(f"  [pipeline] loaded {backbone} on {device} in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s",
              flush=True)
    return _BACKBONES[backbone]


def embed_docs(backend: str, model, tokenizer, device: str,
               docs: Sequence[dg.Doc], batch_size: int = 32,
               max_length: int = 512) -> List[List[Dict]]:
    """Per-document lists of {'token','embedding','label','subword_position'} dicts."""
    toks = [d.words for d in docs]
    labs = [d.token_labels for d in docs]
    if backend == "align":
        import align  # the authors' file, imported unmodified from repo/
        buf = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
            out = align.extract_word_embeddings(
                model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, all_tokens=toks, all_labels=labs,
                model_name="bert-base-cased", device=device)
        return out
    if backend == "batched":
        return eb.extract_word_embeddings(
            model, tokenizer, toks, labs, batch_size=batch_size,
            max_length=max_length, device=device)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown backend {backend!r}")


def run_config(dataset: str, seed: int, backend: str = "batched",
               backbone: str = "bert-base-cased", keep_punct: bool = True,
               l2norm: bool = False, token_auc: str = "micro",
               batch_size: int = 32, max_length: int = 512,
               train_frac: float = 0.5) -> dict:
    """One full TokenCore run: split, embed, fit the memory bank, score, evaluate."""
    tok, model, device = load_backbone(backbone)

    docs = dg.load_dataset(dataset)
    split = dg.split_normal_train(docs, seed=seed, train_frac=train_frac)
    train_docs, test_docs = split.train, split.test

    train_emb = embed_docs(backend, model, tok, device, train_docs, batch_size, max_length)
    test_emb = embed_docs(backend, model, tok, device, test_docs, batch_size, max_length)

    if not keep_punct:
        train_emb = [[it for it in s if not is_punct(it["token"])] for s in train_emb]
        test_emb = [[it for it in s if not is_punct(it["token"])] for s in test_emb]

    X_train, y_train, _, _ = eb.flatten(train_emb)
    X_test, y_test, doc_idx, _ = eb.flatten(test_emb)
    if l2norm:
        X_train = X_train / np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(X_train, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-12)
        X_test = X_test / np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(X_test, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-12)

    det = TokenCoreDetector(n_neighbors=1)
    det.fit(X_train)
    scores = det.decision_function(X_test)

    n_docs = len(test_docs)
    doc_token_scores = [scores[doc_idx == i] for i in range(n_docs)]
    doc_token_labels = [y_test[doc_idx == i] for i in range(n_docs)]
    doc_labels = [d.doc_label for d in test_docs]

    res = ev.evaluate(doc_token_scores, doc_token_labels, doc_labels)
    if token_auc == "macro":
        per_doc = [ev.safe_auc(l, s) for s, l in zip(doc_token_scores, doc_token_labels)
                   if len(np.unique(l)) == 2]
        res["token_auroc"] = float(np.mean(per_doc)) if per_doc else float("nan")
        res["n_docs_with_both_classes"] = len(per_doc)
    res.update({
        "dataset": dataset,
        "seed": seed,
        "backend": backend,
        "backbone": backbone,
        "keep_punct": keep_punct,
        "l2norm": l2norm,
        "token_auc": token_auc,
        "n_train_docs": len(train_docs),
        "n_test_docs": len(test_docs),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(det.n_bank_),
        "n_train_tokens": int(X_train.shape[0]),
        "n_train_anomalous_tokens": int(y_train.sum()),
        "embedding_dim": int(X_train.shape[1]),
        "train_token_stats": dg.token_label_stats(train_docs),
        "test_token_stats": dg.token_label_stats(test_docs),
        "all_token_stats": dg.token_label_stats(docs),
    })
    return res


def summarise(runs: Sequence[dict]) -> dict:
    """Mean/std of the four headline metrics over a list of per-seed runs."""
    keys = ("token_auroc", "token_auprc", "doc_auroc", "doc_auprc")
    out = {}
    for k in keys:
        vals = np.array([r[k] for r in runs], dtype=float)
        out[k] = {"mean": float(np.nanmean(vals)), "std": float(np.nanstd(vals)),
                  "min": float(np.nanmin(vals)), "max": float(np.nanmax(vals)),
                  "n": int(vals.size)}
    out["per_seed"] = [{k: float(r[k]) for k in keys} | {"seed": r["seed"]} for r in runs]
    return out

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The graded run is a faithful, unmodified-wrapper reproduction of TokenCore: released Grammar .npy (validated 300 docs / 30 anomalous), 50%-of-normal train split, BERT-base-uncased last hidden state, element-wise max pooling over subwords (Eq. 1), memory bank of normal-training tokens only (1202 tokens, 0 anomalous), Euclidean 1-NN token score (Eq. 2), arithmetic-mean document aggregation (Eq. 3), pooled token AUROC/AUPRC plus doc-level metrics, all computed live (no paper number appears in the code, random control 0.457, train self-distance ~3e-7). The clean re-run reproduces Grammar token AUROC 0.5978 vs the paper's 0.6371, a 0.039 gap that is outside the stated +/-0.02 band (token AUPRC 0.0346 vs 0.0407 is inside it), so the target value is not matched by this configuration. The most plausible causes are paper-underspecified choices (A1/A3/A5/A8/A9), the documented paper-vs-released-code backbone conflict (uncased vs cased), and single-split randomness on a test set with only 47 positive tokens; there is no evidence of hard-coding, wrong data, or a substituted method/loss. Two caveats worth noting: the graded payload only carries seed 0 although the workspace holds a 10-seed spread (results/spread.json) and a backbone/punctuation/L2/macro config sweep (results/config_sweep.json), so the significance of the residual gap cannot be judged from metrics.json alone, and the Grammar document-level AUROC (0.5121) is far below the paper's 0.6553 (not a contracted claim). The six baselines required by R8 were never run, which does not affect the target C1 value but leaves the paper's 7-method comparison unreproduced.
